title: Correct the cross-domain stitch framing: it is 9,818, not 3
evidence: GQ-010-BASELINE.html §4.2. Measured 9,818 people span >=2 domains against a README claim of 3.

spec.description: The README's most-quoted limitation - 'Cross-domain stitch is 3. Not 3%, three people - Karpathy, Jensen Huang, Simon Willison' - is wrong by 3,272x. The named three are correct but are only the github+youtube pair. The crates_io load added 9,815 crates+github people the README never mentions. This framing was inherited by every downstream document from the Foundry enrichment log onward.
spec.context: Domain pairs: crates+github 9,815; github+youtube_video 3; youtube_channel+youtube_video 1; crates+youtube_video 1; book+anything ZERO. The real limitation is sharper and more interesting than the documented one: BOOKS OVERLAP WITH NOTHING. Zero book+github, zero book+crates. The honest statement is that the corpus splits into a living-software population that stitches well and a dead-books population that cannot stitch at all - which the README's own analysis (20,246 book people died before 1950) explains while its headline number contradicts. Caveat to carry: 9,815 of the 9,818 come from ONE source load and both sides are kind='unknown'-dominated, so this is breadth from one source class, not four, and does not satisfy GQ-010 criterion #1. Measured 2026-08-07 by PG-BASELINE against the shipped graph-v2 asset: people_graph_v2.sqlite, 1,113,350,144 bytes, db SHA-256 9938237a33277fe3a29a278d68c361a1f300d9060740cc2e917920157d9b919b, at repo commit de048bb3b34bf931b56fd741cb46c1334acdfb98.
